title: Pairwise mapping of concatenated lists
statement: Let $g$ be a function of two arguments, let $n,k$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ and $f'$ assign lists to each natural number, with entries in the respective input types of $g$. Suppose every list $f(z)$ and every list $f'(z)$ has length $k$. Applying $g$ entry by entry to the concatenations of $f(0),\ldots,f(n-1)$ and $f'(0),\ldots,f'(n-1)$ gives the concatenation, over $z<n$, of the lists obtained by applying $g$ entry by entry to $f(z)$ and $f'(z)$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ maps a pair of elements from the two entry types to a common type
$f$ maps natural numbers to lists of the first entry type
$f'$ maps natural numbers to lists of the second entry type
